## ✨ Added

- Short links for password-less shares, if you set a server master key. By default a password-less share carries its decryption key in the URL `#fragment`. That keeps the link end-to-end (the server can never decrypt it), but it makes the link long. Set `MASTER_KEY` and password-less uploads switch to a third at-rest mode, server mode: the per-file age key is wrapped with the master key and stored, so the link is just `…/d/aB3xK` with no fragment. The recipient opens the short link and the server decrypts the file with its master key, no credential needed. Password shares are untouched and stay end-to-end.
- `MASTER_KEY` is a new optional environment variable (a masked field in the Unraid template). Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32`. It lives only in the container environment, never in the `/data` volume, so a stolen data backup stays unreadable. Keep it secret and back it up: if you lose it, password-less files can't be recovered. Leave it empty to keep the long `#key` links.
- Template dropdowns: `ENCRYPT_UPLOADS` (`true | false`) and `DEFAULT_EXPIRY` (`7d | 1h | 6h | 1d | 30d | never`) are pick lists in the Unraid template instead of free-text fields.
- Browser-tab favicon: the gold feather shows up in the browser tab (`app/icon.svg`, served automatically by Next.js), centered so it stays legible down to 16×16.

How the modes compare:

| Share type | Key wrapped with | Link | Server can decrypt? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Password | your password | `…/d/<slug>` | No, not even the operator |
| Server (`MASTER_KEY` set, no password) | the server master key | `…/d/<slug>`, short | Yes, it holds the master key. A stolen data backup alone can't. |
| Link (no master key, no password) | key in `#fragment` | `…/d/<slug>#k=…`, long | No, the key never reaches the server |

## 🎨 Design

- Floating glass UI: the upload page is a frosted-glass window floating over a soft gold and violet background. The drop zone sits inside it as a recessed glass well that lights up gold when you drag a file over it.
- The feather takes centre stage: the logo crowns the top of the drop zone, and the header logo and wordmark are larger.
- The accent colour matches the logo: the primary colour is the feather's gold (`#d4af37`) instead of violet, so buttons, the upload progress ring and the copy button all pick it up.
- Sharper copy: the subtitle reads "Encrypted, and gone when it expires." in all 26 languages, and a redundant footer line is gone.

## ⚡ Improved

- With `MASTER_KEY` unset, nothing changes: password-less shares keep their long `#fragment` links. The mode is recorded per file, so stored files keep the mode they were created with.

## 🐛 Fixed

- The copy-link button did nothing over plain HTTP. The browser's Clipboard API only works in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), so at `http://<lan-ip>:3000` the copy failed silently. Copying now falls back to a method that works without HTTPS, and the link field selects itself on focus so you can always copy it by hand.
- Init-log banner: `print-banner.sh` now prints a newline after the shared ASCII banner (the banner file has none of its own), so the `─────` separator sits on its own line instead of running into the banner's last line. The banner subtitle also matches the UI wording ("encrypted, auto-expiring").
